summary.headline: Finolex Cables Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 22% YoY to a record electrical segment INR 1,697 crores, but margins were squeezed by Middle East-driven input costs.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew about 22% YoY and QoQ, with EBITDA up 7% YoY and PAT up 6% YoY, while full-year revenue rose about 19% and PAT about 14%. Management said late-quarter Middle East disruption, rupee depreciation and higher raw material costs left margins slightly under pressure, and inventory was built up by about INR 300 crores. Communication cables grew about 30% YoY in Q4 after flat full-year revenue, helped by hardening fiber prices, while the EHV JV turned profitable. Management declined to give formal guidance, citing volatility in the Middle East situation.

financial_highlights.value: revenue about INR 450 crores, profit about INR 21 crores
about INR 237 crores total; unallocable about INR 224 crores

segments.name: Electrical (wires and cables)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,697 crores, the highest ever; FY26 revenue up about 22%. Auto cables volume up about 30%, flexibles about 17%, power about 21%. Building wire roughly flat in volume; agricultural cables volume down about 15-16%.

segments.name: Communication cables (OFC)
segments.commentary: Full-year revenue flat at about INR 500 crores with about 7% volume growth; Q4 revenue up about 30% YoY and QoQ. About three-fourths of the segment is optic fiber. Fiber draw capacity 4 million km, utilisation about 3.2 million km.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Fans did not grow in volume in FY26 due to unseasonal rains and BIS norm changes causing destocking. PVC conduits running at about 85% utilisation. Management called segment performance under par and is reviewing its portfolio and distribution.

segments.name: EHV JV with Sumitomo
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR 450 crores and profit about INR 21 crores in FY26; started the year with an order book of about INR 380 crores. Key machinery utilisation above 80%.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue about INR 52 crores in FY26 versus about INR 30 crores in FY25; export share about 0.5-1% now, targeted at 2-3% over two years.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management said it would not commit to numbers given Middle East volatility.
Communication cable margins expected to improve beyond FY26's about 6% EBIT; management earlier indicated 8-9% EBIT possible in FY27, subject to no supply constraints.
Preform plant (100 metric ton phase 1) commissioned mid-March 2026; benefits expected from end of Q2 or Q3 FY27. Fiber draw capacity to double from 4 to 8 million km by end Q2 or July/August 2026.
Fixed-price long-term communications contract (over half of OFC capacity) renews end of June 2026; prices expected to be renegotiated.
FY27 capex about INR 300 crores: about INR 200 crores new capacity enhancement (including doubling solar cable capacity) plus about INR 100 crores balance on OFC expansion.
Employee and other expenses as a percentage of sales expected to be similar to FY26 on an annual basis.
Electrical capacity utilisation about 66% at March-end; management sees headroom to about 80-85% without major investment.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR 240 crores, including infusion into the Sumitomo JV.
FY27 capex planned at about INR 300 crores total: about INR 200 crores new capacity and about INR 100 crores to complete OFC expansion.
Fiber draw capacity expansion to 8 million km expected to complete July/August 2026; preform plant phase 1 (100 MT) commissioned mid-March 2026 with 2-3 months stabilisation.
Solar cables launched Q4 FY25 and nearing full capacity; capacity to be doubled.
EHV JV key machinery utilisation above 80%; plan to add capacity to lift overall plant utilisation toward 70-75%.
demand_pricing: Electrical: about 14 price increases during FY26, all upward; effective price change about 24-25% on most electrical SKUs.
Retail vs project mix in electrical wires moved from about 80/20 to about two-thirds retail, one-third project.
Building wire retail demand hit by trade destocking amid copper price volatility; project sales stable.
OFC: fiber prices were low for first 7-8 months of FY26, hardened from end Q3 on data center demand and defence use; supply constrained (germanium, glass, China/Japan capacity blocked).
Military/defence applications constrained by raw material supplier covenants and some government export restrictions on raw materials.

qa_highlights.question: How should we see communication cable growth and margins by FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit to a number; said margins should improve beyond FY26's about 6% EBIT, but supply chain and Middle East uncertainty limit visibility.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EHV JV growth path to FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Turned profitable with order blend of supply and turnkey; market size about USD 0.5-0.75 billion now, potentially USD 4-5 billion in 3-4 years; competitors adding similar vertical insulation technology.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 communication margin improvement from mix or pricing, and will fixed contracts limit benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin improvement from a few orders taken at current prices beyond the long-term contract; benefit from higher fiber prices to appear around Q2 as contracts renew.

qa_highlights.question: Electrical capacity utilisation and maximum revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation about 66% at March-end; practical maximum about 80-85%, implying about 15% revenue headroom at current prices without major capex.

qa_highlights.question: OFC draw capacity, utilisation and EBIT target?
qa_highlights.answer: Current draw capacity 4 million km, utilisation about 3.2 million km; capacity to reach 8 million km by end Q2 or July/August. Management said 9% EBIT in FY27 possible subject to no supply constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Exports and FMEG outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports about INR 52 crores in FY26 with export share targeted at 2-3% in two years. FMEG performance under par; portfolio, team and distribution being reworked.

risks_watch: Germanium and glass (preform inputs) supply constraints from China and Europe, with export restrictions; inventory covers only a few months.
Middle East conflict driving raw material and freight costs; rupee depreciation; about INR 300 crores extra inventory built up with pass-through timing uncertain.
Fixed-price OFC contract renewal at end June 2026 and pricing reset in the next tender cycle.
Defence and military demand constrained by supplier covenants and export restrictions.
Retail channel destocking in building wires and fans after BIS norm changes; agricultural cable volumes down about 15-16%.
Preform plant stabilisation and fiber draw expansion timelines (Q2/Q3 FY27).
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and capacity growth in OFC and EHV, but cautious and evasive on numbers: management declined to give guidance or margin targets, repeatedly citing Middle East and supply chain volatility.
key_quotes: Revenue for Quarter-4 was up by about 22%, both year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter.
I think we should do better than that.
I actually do not give out any guidance, especially in a situation like today, where you do not know whether the war is ending tomorrow.

growth.why: No formal guidance given due to Middle East volatility; only communication segment margin expected to beat FY26's ~6% EBIT (no number), backed by fiber draw capacity doubling to 8 million km by July/August 2026, preform plant commissioned, and ~INR 300 cr FY27 capex with electrical utilisation at 66% leaving headroom.
